. Radiant App

🔗 https://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/radiant.html

App: Radiant

Application Task

The Radiant app is used for business analytics and statistical analysis. It allows users to explore datasets, perform statistical tests, build models, and visualize data interactively through a web interface.

Users can:

Upload and explore datasets

Perform descriptive statistics

Run regression models

Conduct clustering or factor analysis

Visualize results using charts and tables

Radiant is designed to help business decision-making using data analysis tools.

Data Information Presented

The app presents several types of information, such as:

Summary statistics (mean, median, variance)

Data tables and distributions

Regression models and prediction results

Correlation between variables

Cluster or segmentation analysis

Graphs and plots for visualization

These results update interactively when inputs change, helping users explore data quickly.

Insights Observed

After exploring the results, several insights can be generated:

Relationships between variables can be identified easily.

Trends or patterns in business data become visible through charts.

Predictive models can estimate future outcomes.

Clustering helps identify customer segments or groups.

Overall, Radiant demonstrates how R can be used for interactive data analysis and decision-making.

2. Google Charts App

🔗 https://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/google-charts.html

Application Task

This Shiny app demonstrates how Google Charts visualization tools can be integrated with R to create interactive dashboards and charts.

The main task of this application is to visualize data dynamically using different chart types.

Examples include:

Line charts

Bar charts

Pie charts

Area charts

Scatter plots

Users can interact with the charts and change parameters to see different visualizations.

Data Information Presented

The app displays information such as:

Category comparisons (bar charts)

Trends over time (line charts)

Percentage distributions (pie charts)

Relationships between variables (scatter plots)

These visualizations help users understand patterns and relationships in data.

Insights Observed

From the generated charts we can observe:

Visual trends and patterns are easier to understand.

Data comparisons between categories become clearer.

Interactive visualization improves data exploration.

Users can quickly detect anomalies or patterns.

This demonstrates how R Shiny can create interactive dashboards for data visualization and reporting.

3. Overall Discussion (Summary)

Exploring the Shiny gallery shows that R can be used to build interactive data science applications.

Examples include:

Business analytics tools

Data dashboards

Statistical analysis platforms

Interactive visualizations

Using Shiny, analysts can transform R scripts into web applications that allow users to interact with data and models in real time.

✅ Short conclusion for your assignment

R Shiny applications like Radiant and Google Charts show how R can be used to build interactive data science tools. Radiant focuses on statistical analysis and business decision-making, while Google Charts demonstrates interactive data visualization. These apps help users explore data, identify patterns, and generate insights more effectively.
